title: The Lighter Brief
overview: This edition has a bit of everything: a big staffing shake-up at the White House after the midterms, some handy money-saving travel tips for Charlotte folks, and a feel-good win for wildlife in northern England. There's also a long-running study that coffee lovers will enjoy, with a sensible caveat attached.

stories.headline: Fort Mill solar plant gets ready to restart
stories.summary: Silfab Solar says it will restart its chemical commissioning process at its Fort Mill, South Carolina plant on Monday. That work has been paused since March, after two chemical leaks at the site. The company says it completed a thorough review of the facility and its procedures before deciding to resume.
key_facts: Silfab gave the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services a 72-hour notice on Friday
Commissioning restarts Monday after a pause since March
The company says restarting commissioning doesn't mean manufacturing begins right away
stories.why: Neighbors who have followed the plant since the March leaks will want to know that activity is picking back up.

stories.headline: Stephen Miller named White House chief of staff
stories.summary: After Republicans lost control of Congress in Tuesday's midterms, President Trump named longtime adviser Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff. Wiles resigned Thursday night. Trump says he can work with Democrats on issues like immigration and taxes. Many observers see Miller, a key architect of the administration's immigration policies, as a sign of a more combative approach. Democratic leaders and Republican Sen. Thom Tillis criticized the choice.
key_facts: Miller, 41, was deputy chief of staff for policy in Trump's second term
Wiles co-managed Trump's 2024 campaign and was seen as a steadying presence
Trump called Miller an 'MVP' and 'very loyal'
Sen. Tillis (R-N.C.) called Miller the 'worst of all possible choices' for the role
stories.why: The chief of staff is the president's gatekeeper and main negotiator with Congress, so this pick will shape how Washington works now that Democrats control Congress.

stories.headline: Macklemore says US arenas won't host his Palestine benefit tour
stories.summary: Macklemore posted on Instagram that nine major US arenas turned down his Free Palestine benefit shows after first offering available dates. His European leg in Dublin, Paris and London raised money for medical, food and educational aid for Palestinians. He says US shows will still happen, possibly outdoors or in other venues.
key_facts: Named venues include Madison Square Garden, Barclays Center, Chase Center and Climate Pledge Arena
The European tour opened Oct. 26 in Dublin and ended Oct. 30 at London's OVO Arena Wembley
No US dates have been announced yet
disputed: The claim that arenas withdrew dates because of the cause is Macklemore's own account and hasn't been confirmed by the venues
He didn't describe any shared written policy, and the venues have separate owners
An MSG Entertainment spokesperson responded to Rolling Stone, pointing to how busy its venues are
stories.why: It's a live debate about who gets a stage, and fans who want US dates now know where things stand.

stories.headline: Montego Bay school and students disagree over sick-day cause
stories.summary: Several girls at Mount Alvernia High in Montego Bay got sick this week, with vomiting among the symptoms, and some students blame the canteen. Principal Kayon Whyne says the Ministry of Health cleared the canteen. She suggests water-borne illness after recent flooding, or a flu, could be the cause instead. The affected grades moved to online classes as a precaution.
key_facts: Grades 7 to 9 were affected and moved online; grades 10 to 13 were not
Classes were dismissed early Thursday
The school's email to students mentioned suspected gastroenteritis
disputed: The cause hasn't been publicly confirmed. Students question the canteen, while the principal says health officials cleared it
stories.why: Parents in the area will want to watch for clearer answers on what made students ill.

links.title: Mount Alvernia High principal denies canteen food made students ill

stories.headline: Call for calmer debate in Jamaica's Parliament
stories.summary: A heated exchange broke out in Jamaica's House of Representatives after Tuesday's sitting and was broadcast live. A UWI government lecturer is now urging tougher penalties for MPs who break the rules, such as suspensions or fines. MP Mikael Phillips has apologized and says he reacted to remarks about his late mother. MP Desmond McKenzie says he has nothing to apologize for.
key_facts: The exchange began when Phillips confronted House Speaker Juliet Holness after adjournment
Lecturer Damion Gordon suggested suspensions or financial penalties
McKenzie addressed the matter at a JLP press conference on Friday
stories.why: How lawmakers treat each other sets the tone for public life, and the conversation could lead to new rules.

links.title: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns

stories.headline: Free flu shots available across Jamaica
stories.summary: Jamaica is in the middle of flu season, and health officials are encouraging people to get vaccinated. The shot is free at public health centres and hospitals for priority groups, and anyone else can get it privately for a fee. Officials also recommend covering coughs and sneezes.
key_facts: Flu season typically runs from October to March and can last into May
Priority groups include pregnant women, healthcare workers, people 65 and older with chronic conditions, and children six months and older with chronic illnesses
Annual vaccination is recommended
stories.why: It's an easy, free step that can help keep you and the people around you healthier this season.

links.title: Jamaicans encouraged to get Flu vaccine

stories.headline: I-77 toll lane project is back, and NCDOT wants your input
stories.summary: The revived I-77 toll lane project south of Charlotte is in its early stages, with construction not expected until the 2030s. NCDOT Secretary Daniel Johnson says the community will help shape it. A community hub is open on weekdays for feedback on design and on ideas like toll caps and free rides for cars with three or more people.
key_facts: The design is only 10% to 15% complete
At least $300 million in community benefits is tied to the project
Charlotte City Council votes Monday on a working group to oversee those benefits
Four developers are competing for the project
stories.why: Residents have a real early chance to weigh in, and the benefits could help fund things like a grocery store off West Boulevard.

links.title: NCDOT outlines next steps for revived I-77 toll lane project

stories.headline: Opinion: Are Trump and Nicki Minaj's best moments behind them?
stories.summary: A Newsweek analysis argues that President Trump and Nicki Minaj, two famous Queens natives who appeared together at a Treasury event in January, still have huge audiences but less power to set trends. The author points to the midterm results as a sign of Trump's waning influence. This is an opinion piece, not news reporting.
key_facts: Minaj has 224 million Instagram followers
The two met at a Treasury Department event in January 2026
The midterms were held November 3
disputed: This is one writer's argument and interpretation, not established fact
stories.why: It's a lighter take on how fame and political influence change over time.

links.title: Nicki Minaj Is the Logical Conclusion of Trump: Passé
